items.title: Colucci v. Colucci
items.says: In Colucci v. Colucci, the Supreme Court of Canada set out the framework for a payor's application under s. 17 of the Divorce Act to retroactively decrease child support: a past material change in circumstances, a presumed start date at effective notice (up to three years before formal notice), discretion to depart from it, and recalculation under the Guidelines; effective notice requires disclosure of supporting documents.

source.expect: to retroactively decrease child support

review.problem: Para. 113 sets out only the framework for a payor's application to retroactively decrease child support; rescinding arrears is dealt with elsewhere in the decision.

items.title: Kerr v. Baranow
items.says: The Supreme Court of Canada set out how unjust enrichment claims between unmarried partners are decided, including the joint family venture.

source.expect: joint family venture

items.title: Moge v. Moge
items.says: The Supreme Court of Canada held that spousal support under the Divorce Act is to compensate for economic disadvantages from the marriage and its breakdown, not only to promote self-sufficiency.

source.expect: fair and equitable distribution of resources

items.title: Miglin v. Miglin
items.says: The Supreme Court of Canada set out the two-stage approach for deciding whether to make a spousal support order that is different from what a separation agreement says.

source.expect: circumstances in which the agreement was negotiated and executed

items.title: Hryniak v. Mauldin
items.says: In Hryniak v. Mauldin, the Supreme Court of Canada said there is no genuine issue requiring a trial when the judge can reach a fair and just decision on the merits on a summary judgment motion: when the process lets the judge make the necessary findings of fact, apply the law to the facts, and is a proportionate, quicker and less expensive way to a just result.

source.expect: no genuine issue requiring a trial

items.title: Who can serve the application

source.expect: shall be carried out by a person other than the party

items.title: Order that service is not required

source.expect: order that service is not required

items.title: Exemption from the information program
items.says: The court can, on motion, order that the information program requirements do not apply to a party because of urgency or hardship or for another reason in the interest of justice.

source.expect: because of urgency or hardship or for some other reason

items.title: Costs when a claim is withdrawn

source.expect: shall pay the costs of every other party

items.title: Splitting the divorce from other issues
items.says: On motion, the court can split the divorce from the other issues so the divorce can be granted first, if neither spouse will be disadvantaged and reasonable arrangements have been made for the support of any children.

source.expect: splitting a divorce from the other issues

items.title: Joint divorce application

source.expect: only with the consent of both spouses

items.title: Marriage certificate and divorce registry report
items.says: The court does not grant a divorce until a marriage certificate (or an explanation why it is impractical to get one) and a report from the Central Registry of Divorce Proceedings have been filed.

source.expect: Central Registry of Divorce Proceedings

items.title: Motion with notice: serving and filing

items.title: Order made without notice comes back to court

source.expect: within 14 days or on a date chosen by the court

items.title: Stopping repeated motions
items.says: If a party tries to delay the case, add to its costs or otherwise abuse the process by making many motions without merit, the court can order that the party not make any more motions without the court's permission.

source.expect: making numerous motions without merit

items.title: Talking before a conference

source.expect: decide a question of law before trial

items.title: Payor's answer to a default hearing: 10 days
items.says: Within 10 days after being served with a notice of default hearing, the payor serves on the recipient and files a financial statement (Form 13) and a default dispute (Form 30B).

source.expect: Within 10 days after being served with the notice

review.problem: The presumption that the payor admits the statement of money owed is r. 30(6), not 30(3).

items.title: Orders at a default hearing
items.says: At a default hearing, if the payor does not show an inability to pay, the court can order payment of arrears and future support on terms and can order imprisonment, continuous or intermittent, for no more than 180 days or until the arrears are paid. Imprisonment does not cancel the arrears.

source.expect: which shall not be more than 180 days

items.title: First notice before licence suspension
items.says: When a support order filed with the Family Responsibility Office is in default, the Director can serve a first notice saying the payor's driver's licence may be suspended unless, within 30 days, the payor makes a satisfactory arrangement, files an order to refrain, or pays all arrears.

source.expect: may serve a first notice on the payor

items.title: Payor about to leave Ontario
items.says: The Ontario Court of Justice or the Family Court can issue a warrant for a payor's arrest if the payor is about to leave Ontario and there are reasonable grounds to believe they intend to evade their support obligations.

source.expect: the payor is about to leave Ontario

items.title: Stopping a payor from hiding assets
items.says: A court, including the Ontario Court of Justice, can make an order restraining the disposal or wasting of assets that may hinder or defeat enforcement of a support order.

source.expect: restraining the disposition or wasting of assets

items.title: How much of wages can be garnished for support
items.says: When support is being enforced, 50 per cent of a person's wages are exempt from seizure or garnishment, so up to half can be taken. A judge can change the exemption.

source.expect: Fifty per cent of a person’s wages are exempt

items.title: Orders when a person is in contempt
items.says: If the court finds a person in contempt, it can order imprisonment on just terms, a fine, a payment to a party as a penalty, that the person do or not do something, costs, and obedience to any other order. The court can suspend imprisonment or a fine on conditions.

source.expect: be imprisoned for any period and on any conditions that are just

items.title: Approaching dismissal in the Ontario Court of Justice
items.says: In the Ontario Court of Justice, the clerk serves a notice of approaching dismissal (Form 39) by mail or email if the case has not been settled, withdrawn, or scheduled or adjourned for trial before the 365th day after it started, unless that time was lengthened by order.

source.expect: notice of approaching dismissal (Form

review.problem: r. 40(5) only requires the notice; dismissal unless a party acts within 60 days is r. 40(6).

items.title: Setting aside a clerk's dismissal
items.says: The case management judge or another judge can, on motion, set aside an order of the clerk dismissing the case.

source.expect: set aside an order of the clerk

items.title: Answering a rule 1.4 notice: 15 days
items.says: After a notice that a case may be stayed or dismissed as frivolous, vexatious or an abuse of process, the party who brought it can file a written submission of no more than 10 pages within 15 days. If none is filed, the court can make the order without further notice.

source.expect: No later than 15 days after receiving the notice

items.title: Breaking an exclusive possession order
items.says: A person who contravenes an order for exclusive possession of the matrimonial home commits a provincial offence, with a fine of up to $5,000 or up to three months in jail for a first offence, and more for later offences.

source.expect: contravenes an order for exclusive possession is guilty

items.title: Restraining order forms (25F, 25G, 25H)
items.says: A restraining order under the Family Law Act or the Children's Law Reform Act is prepared by the clerk as soon as it is made, in Form 25F or 25G. An order ending a restraining order is in Form 25H.

source.expect: shall be in Form 25F or 25G

items.title: Who must prove a relocation is best (Children's Law Reform Act)
items.says: If the parties substantially follow an order or agreement giving the child substantially equal time with each, the party who wants to relocate the child must prove the move is in the child's best interests.

source.expect: the party who intends to relocate the child has the burden

items.title: Objecting to a relocation under the Divorce Act: 30 days
items.says: Under the Divorce Act, the person who gave notice can relocate the child as of the date in the notice if a court authorizes it, or if no person with parenting time or decision-making responsibility objects within 30 days after receiving the notice (in the prescribed form or by application) and no order prohibits the relocation.

source.expect: does not object to the relocation within 30 days

review.problem: Drops the alternative in s. 16.91(1)(a): a relocation authorized by a court may go ahead on the notice date regardless of an objection, so 'unless ... objects' overstates the effect of an objection.

items.title: Change in circumstances: spousal support
items.says: Before changing a spousal support order under the Divorce Act, the court must be satisfied that there has been a change in the condition, means, needs or other circumstances of either former spouse since the order or the last change.

source.expect: a change in the condition, means, needs or other circumstances

items.title: Form 15D: consent motion to change child support
items.says: When the parties and any assignee agree to change only a child support obligation, they file a consent motion to change child support (Form 15D) with its attachments, five copies of a draft order, stamped envelopes, a support deduction order information form and a draft support deduction order.

source.expect: consent motion to change child support (Form 15D)

review.problem: r. 15(18) lists what is filed with a Form 15D consent (draft orders, envelopes, a support deduction order information form and a draft support deduction order); that no financial statements are needed comes from r. 13(4.2), not rule 15.

items.title: Serving a motion to change
items.says: The motion to change and its attachments, with a blank response (Form 15B) and a blank consent (Form 15C), are served by special service, not regular service.

source.expect: shall be served by special service

items.title: If no response to a motion to change
items.says: If the other party does not serve a response or return a consent, the party making the motion to change can file a motion form (Form 14B) asking the court to make the order requested, unless an assignee opposes.

source.expect: may file a motion form (Form 14B) asking that the court make the order

items.title: D.B.S. v. S.R.G.
items.says: The Supreme Court of Canada set out how courts decide retroactive child support, including that retroactive awards are not only for exceptional cases, and that delay by the recipient and blameworthy conduct by the payor are relevant.

source.decision: D.B.S. v. S.R.G.; L.J.W. v. T.A.R.; Henry v. Henry; Hiemstra v. Hiemstra, 2006 SCC 37
source.expect: retroactive awards cannot simply be regarded as exceptional orders

items.title: Bracklow v. Bracklow
items.says: The Supreme Court of Canada recognized three bases for spousal support entitlement: compensatory, contractual and non-compensatory (based on need).

source.expect: three conceptual bases for entitlement to spousal support

items.title: Rick v. Brandsema
items.says: In Rick v. Brandsema, the Supreme Court of Canada held that separating spouses negotiating an agreement have a duty to make full and honest disclosure of all relevant financial information, and that a deliberate failure to disclose may make the agreement open to court intervention where the resulting settlement is substantially at variance from the objectives of the governing legislation.

source.expect: full and honest disclosure of all relevant financial information

review.problem: Drops the condition in Rick para. 47: a deliberate failure to disclose may make the agreement vulnerable to judicial intervention only where the resulting settlement is substantially at variance from the objectives of the governing legislation.

items.title: Carey v. Laiken
items.says: The Supreme Court of Canada set out what must be proved for civil contempt: a clear order, actual knowledge of it, and an intentional act or failure to act that breaches it, each proved beyond a reasonable doubt.

source.expect: beyond a reasonable doubt
